Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II report + audit period clarification

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. We’re starting our security review for an upcoming platform procurement and need to confirm a couple of items before we proceed: 

1) Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report for the last 12 months (or a recent audit period) you can share?
2) If the report isn’t public, do you provide a bridge letter that explains changes in coverage or timing? If so, what format do you provide (PDF + signature, or statement on letterhead)?
3) What is your audited period (start/end dates) for the most recent Type II? We need dates to confirm overlap with our security window.

If there are standard templates or a checklist you prefer we follow when requesting evidence, that would be helpful. Also, can you confirm secure transfer options (SFTP, pre-signed S3, or Google Drive links) and any redaction guidance you recommend?

Our target procurement review date is the week of July 2 — if you can let us know availability and an expected turnaround, we’ll plan accordingly.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II report + audit period clarification

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and a couple of options so you can pick what fits your process.

Summary:
- We have a SOC 2 Type II report issued for the period 2027-05-01 through 2028-04-30 (covers our hosted API + core control set).
- We can provide either the full PDF report under an NDA or a signed bridge letter if you need a short-form attestation.
- Secure transfer: presigned S3 links (preferred), encrypted SFTP, or shared Drive folder with restricted access are all possible.

What we typically share:
- Full Type II report PDF (redaction available on request) — requires a simple NDA and access list.
- Bridge letter (one-page PDF on letterhead) — summarizes the audit period, scope, and any coverage notes. Good when a full report isn’t needed.
- Control crosswalk (CSV) mapping common SIG/CAIQ questions to report sections — helpful for faster reviews.

Attachments (attached to this reply):
- SOC2_Type_II_Request_Guide.docx — describes our preferred intake flow and sample NDA language.
- sample_bridge_letter.pdf — example of the one-page bridge we can provide.
- redaction_guidance.txt — short notes on what we typically redact (personal data, internal IP where applicable).

Two delivery paths (pick one):
A) Full report delivery: sign our standard recipient NDA (we can share DocuSign link), we provision a presigned S3 link valid 7 days. Expect delivery within 2 business days after NDA is complete.
B) Bridge letter + control crosswalk: we can email the signed bridge letter and crosswalk within 24 hours; no NDA required for the bridge letter itself but full report access will still require NDA.

If you need a redacted copy, let us know the categories, and we’ll prepare that in the initial package (add 1 business day).

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell us which path (A or B) you prefer.
2) If A, we’ll send a DocuSign NDA and an intake form (minimal).
3) If B, we’ll send the signed bridge + crosswalk and confirm secure transfer method.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call today or tomorrow to confirm. 

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOC2_Type_II_Request_Guide.docx (DOCX), sample_bridge_letter.pdf (PDF), redaction_guidance.txt (TXT)

Thanks Kim — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we pick a path: 

- Our audit window requires coverage that includes at least part of June 2028. Your audited period ends 2028-04-30 — would you be able to provide an interim bridge that states no significant control changes occurred since the audit end date, or do you have a subsequent monitoring letter?
- For the full report path (A), can you confirm how long the presigned S3 link stays valid and whether access is logged (we require audit logs for evidence downloads)?
- For redaction guidance: we typically ask vendors to redact internal employee IDs and any customer-identifying strings. Your redaction guidance file looks useful — does Redwood apply redactions internally or do you expect customers to redact after download?

If bridge letters can explicitly state no material changes since 2028-04-30 and are signed on letterhead, that will meet our procurement review. Given the timing, path B would be our preferred option if the bridge can include the wording above.

Can we lock in delivery for the bridge letter + crosswalk by end of day Monday (2028-06-19)? I can also schedule a 20-min call if necessary.

Thanks — Maya
